identity.title: Towards a Complete Logical Framework for GNN Expressiveness

problem.claim: The paper seeks a comprehensive, systematic relationship between GNN architectures and logical expressiveness.

gap.claim: High-order WL tests can obscure which graph patterns they capture, while existing work has only explored parts of the relationship between GNNs and logic.

contributions.claim: A framework for identifying logical formulas equivalent to arbitrary GNN architectures.
An analysis of multiple prominent GNN classes that unifies different subareas within the proposed framework.
A logical examination and general determination method for homomorphism expressivity of arbitrary GNN models, addressing several open problems.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present a comprehensive framework intended to explain existing GNN models and inspire future research, including a general method for determining arbitrary models' homomorphism expressivity.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report analyzing multiple classes of prominent GNNs as case studies within the framework.
The authors report a detailed logical examination of homomorphism expressivity and addressing several open problems.

narrative_sequence.summary: GNN expressiveness is important, and WL tests have traditionally served as its primary measure.
High-order WL tests may obscure the graph patterns they capture; prior work has therefore examined GNN expressiveness through first-order logic.
The paper proposes a systematic GNN–logic framework covering arbitrary architectures and intended to explain existing models.
The framework is applied to prominent GNN classes and to homomorphism expressivity, with a general determination method and discussion of open problems.

source_observation.claim: The paper uses logical formulas as an explicit explanatory interface for arbitrary GNN architectures, then applies that interface to model classes and homomorphism expressivity.

lessons.interpretation: An explicit intermediate representation can make expressiveness claims more interpretable and comparable across model families.
lessons.application: When introducing a new architecture, specify the logical formula or fragment it corresponds to and use that correspondence to organize comparisons.
lessons.exception: This move may be unsuitable when the architecture lacks a tractable or well-defined logical characterization.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the exact logical language, formulas, GNN classes, open problems, or conditions under which the proposed correspondences hold.
No quantitative experimental results or independently verified proof details are provided in the abstract.
